correctness.rationale: For the normalized Gaussian restriction the squared centered L2 energy equals I_0(4/sigma^2)/I_0(2/sigma^2)^2-1 exactly. Gaussian/Laplace asymptotics give sigma E(sigma)→sqrt(2π), and positivity plus continuity make the bound global on (0,1]. Centered singleton terms are orthogonal, yielding the two-sided sum bound and both directions of fourth-root summability. The three power-weight constants follow from rigorous dominated convergence, logarithmic harmonic splitting and dominated Riemann-sum convergence. Independence supplies the exact constant-input variance identity. Finite numerical checks are supplemental only.

value.rationale: The sharp iff threshold resolves whether a natural sufficient weight-decay hypothesis of the motivating quasi-interpolation bound is necessary for its own Gaussian singleton construction, rather than merely a proof device. The exact p=4 logarithmic boundary and p<4 integral constant reveal unavoidable additional sample cost at increasing dimension, already for constant data. This is a mathematically motivated parameter boundary and directly interpretable sampling-noise obstruction, not just a renamed textbook inequality.
